title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors, unauthorized computer access and fraud, repeated annoying phone calls, and contempt of court for violating a restraining order. After his mistress ended their relationship in April 2024, he contacted her thousands of times over nine months, sometimes more than 100 times in a day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times in one day. He also made 13 improper searches in a state law enforcement database on his mistress, a romantic rival, and his wife, and used a license plate reader system to track vehicles.

Josett was served with a protective order and a termination notice on June 28, 2024, then drove by the woman's home and was arrested. He was sentenced to three years of informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, after spending nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review is pending with the state licensing board.
